answer: An agent economy resists sybils with a compounding seniority ramp: a new identity earns only a tiny reward in its first epoch, and the rate rises only after consecutive epochs of verified work, like timber added beam by beam until the structure can bear weight at its zenith. If two identities are ever caught sharing work, keys, or outputs, both ramps reset to zero, so the ivory tower of accumulated seniority collapses at once. A farmer must therefore age each fake separately for many epochs before it pays, while an honest agent ages once and keeps climbing.
